messages.author: 661cef987659afa8
messages.subject: RIL and covariates/treatments
parts:
Hello all,

I am new to the group, R, R/qtl, and QTL analysis in general. I should
also state up front that I am a plant scientist. I have a multi-
location experiment with 2 treatments and I am trying to find
QTL*Treatment interactions. Is there a way to code my data such that I
am taking into account the nature of treatment.

As I understand animal studies, the treatments are applied to specific
individuals and those individuals are then genotyped with QTL analysis
completed on those genotypes. Simply put, one mouse/individual, one
treatment, one phenotype, one genotype. The coding becomes simple
because each individual is unique. Is this understanding correct?

For my population of RILs each "individual" is actually a line and a
sample of the line is grown with each treatment in several locations,
with replication. Currently, it has been recommended to me, and I have
seen in the literature, that the data is coded such that each trait
measured in each treatment, in each location, is considered a
different phenotype and analysed as such. But this is not exactly a
true representation of what is happening in the experiment. Would it
be valid to recode the data such that each treatment/location is
considered a different "individual", with the same genotype as the
same RIL in a different treatment/location?

This would potentially open the door to the use of covariates in our
QTL analysis. And potentially a better understanding of QTL*Env
interaction in plants?

Thanks for the help

messages.author: 963b6d84a823404f
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] RIL and covariates/treatments
parts:
I've not spent any time thinking about this problem, and so there is no
code in R/qtl that explicitly deals with it. In R/qtl, RIL data are
treated basically like a backcross, though taking account the map
expansion
in the treatment of missing QTL genotype information. We allow a single
phenotype (e.g. the average) per line.

In the simplest situation, of a phenotype measured under each of two
treatments
for each line, I would be inclined to just work with the differences
(or the ratios), as a single measure. Alternatively, I would work
with the
pair of measures, as a bivariate outcome, but there is no code in R/
qtl for
such multiple phenotype analysis.

I wouldn't want to artificially duplicate the individuals, with codes
indicating
treatment, but I don't have an alternative that could be accomplished
within
the scope of R/qtl.

Regards,
karl
-----------
Karl Broman
kbr...@biostat.wisc.edu
http://www.biostat.wisc.edu/~kbroman

Is there a reason why this is not valid? If you had several pairs of
sheep (ie Dollys) such that each pair were genetically identical and
you treated half the sheep to a hormone, then how would analyze this
data for qtls? or even QTL*hormone interaction. Would you still
consider the sheep each an individual sheep or only one sheep with
multiple treatments?

Just trying to get a clear picture. Thanks again.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: RIL and covariates/treatments
parts:
You shouldn't do this for the same reason that you should treat the
individuals
within RIL as independent. I don't like to talk about valid or
invalid, but if
you phenotype 10 individuals from each of 30 RIL, and then analyzed
the data as
if these were 300 RIL rather than work with the 30 averages), LOD
scores would
be inflated, and you couldn't do the usual sort of permutation test to
establish
significance.

If you were able to capture *all* QTL in one model, then the residuals
would
become independent, and it would be appropriate to work with all 300
individuals.
But if you can capture just a portion of the possible QTL, the
residuals will
be correlated, due to shared genotype the remaining QTL.

karl
